description: Residual-brand allowlist for the Phaneris fork. Every entry is a deliberate, reasoned exception to 'no upstream identifier remains'. The scanner in scripts/check-identity.ts fails a --strict run on any hit that no rule covers, and reports rules that no longer match anything so stale entries get deleted instead of accumulating. Add a rule only when the legacy string must genuinely stay: upstream attribution, historical records, the migration input path, or the identity/scan machinery itself.

rules.reason: Declares the legacy identifiers on purpose: the migration path and the residual scanner both read them from here.
The residual scanner itself; necessarily names every legacy token it searches for.
This allowlist; its reasons quote the tokens they exempt.
The fork plan quotes upstream identifiers and the rejected working names as source material.
Phase A report: the reference inventory and namespace verification record are about the upstream identifiers.
Upstream attribution. Apache-2.0 requires it to survive the rebrand verbatim.
License text and any copyright line; not a rebrand target.
Historical release notes describe what actually shipped under the upstream name; rewriting them would falsify the record.

The one place a legacy environment prefix is still read: a shell profile's CRAFT_WH_* webhook secrets keep working for one transition, with a deprecation notice. The literal only appears in a comment and in the LEGACY_IDENTITY-derived constant.
Reads the legacy GitHub Actions secret as a fallback so CI keeps working until the repository secret itself is renamed — an external operation this change cannot perform.
Documents the CRAFT_WH_* migration path for user-authored shell profiles and automation scripts.
Its header documents why the upstream CRAFT_CONFIG_DIR is deliberately NOT read; naming it is the point of the comment.

The upstream trademark policy still governs the Craft and Craft Agents marks, which this fork must keep honouring. It needs a Phaneris section before release (tracked in the B-phase record) but must not be rewritten to erase the upstream marks.
Historical audit of the upstream codebase under its own name; a record of what was reviewed, not a product surface.
Package guidance that must keep naming the legacy identifiers and the upstream Craft service when explaining what not to rename.

Maintainer documentation: architecture notes, fork records, plans and assessments that describe the fork lineage and quote upstream identifiers as source material. The user-facing documentation set — apps/electron/resources/docs/**, which is synced into the user's data directory and read by the agent — is deliberately NOT covered here.

Vendored 664 KB bundle with no buildable source in this repository, so its strings cannot be regenerated here. One user-visible message still says 'Craft Agent settings'; removing it requires rebuilding the bundle from its own upstream package. Recorded as remaining work in the B-phase record rather than patched by hand, which would only hide that the bundle needs regenerating.
Generated from phaneris.identity.json — contains the LEGACY_IDENTITY block by construction.
Generated — the copyright line credits the upstream copyright holder, which is intentional.
